items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Harry told me that Johnny Mandel heard his record... he didn’t know him

ctx.x: Well, that’s positive. I’m glad to hear that. You’ve worked with, gee, about the greatest in the business, and the list keeps coming. And I’m really glad to see some of the younger players coming, Harry Allen and those guys, embracing this kind of music and keeping it alive.

Harry told me that Johnny Mandel heard his record, called him on the phone, he didn’t know him, called him on the phone and left a message on his answering machine saying he’d heard his CD and said how he was much relieved to know that jazz was in the hands of young players like him and how good it made him feel, which was a great day for Harry. But it’s true. I mean you think that — I remember when Scott Hamilton came around for the first time. And nobody remembers particularly what was going on, now, at the…
